Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly development-server debug page can reflect unencoded exception text, allowing cross-origin script injection through the unauthenticated `/_framework/debug` endpoint used by `dotnet watch`. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69802 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.12 | 10.0.13 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.31 | 8.0.32 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Server) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.20 | 9.0.21 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-96230](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-96230) ### Acknowledgements - Kevin Gosse ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The Blazor WebAssembly debug proxy evaluates debugger expressions by generating and compiling C# source. Certain values originating in the application being debugged, including `ToString()` results, descriptions, and class names, are embedded in that generated source without consistent escaping. We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 2. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc2).

This is our second of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/msbuild.md)

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

Events.RelatedBody:
Originally reported as [a VS feedback issue](https://developercommunity.visualstudio.com/t/Visual-Studio-Razor-formatting-throws-Re/11164071)

A Razor document with an attribute spanning multiple lines, like below, causes the Razor formatter to error:

```
    @attribute [Obsolete("message",
                    error:false)]
``

I'm not sure that should be allowed (I think `@attribute` is defined as a single line directive) but that's besides the point.

### Describe the bug

If a disposable is passed to a primary constructor that stores it, CA2000 reports a leak where the disposable is created. That's true whether it's stored through a property initializer, a field initializer or a captured parameter. The same code with an explicit constructor reports nothing. This looks like the CA2000 counterpart of dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#7803 (CA2213): the analyzer doesn't see the primary constructor's initializers when it follows the call into the constructor.

### Steps to reproduce

.editorconfig: `dotnet_diagnostic.CA2000.severity = warning`

```csharp
public sealed class Res : IDisposable { public void Dispose() { } }

public sealed class Explicit
{
    public Explicit(Res r) { R = r; }
    public Res R { get; }
}

public sealed class PrimaryProperty(Res r) { public Res R { get; } = r; }
public sealed class PrimaryField(Res r) { private readonly Res _r = r; public Res R => _r; }
public sealed class PrimaryCaptured(Res r) { public Res R => r; }

public static class Use
{
    public static Explicit A() => new(new Res());        // no diagnostic
    public static PrimaryProperty B() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
    public static PrimaryField C() => new(new Res());    // CA2000
    public static PrimaryCaptured D() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
}
```

### Expected behavior

None of the four call sites gets a diagnostic. In each case the object is handed to the new instance, which stores it.

### Actual behavior

B, C and D report CA2000: Call `System.IDisposable.Dispose` on object created by 'new Res()' before all references to it are out of scope. A doesn't.

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

Use an explicit constructor, or suppress CA2000 at the call site.

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: EnC: adding an async lambda that awaits a `dynamic` call throws InvalidOperationException in DeltaMetadataWriter.GetFieldDefinitionHandle
Issues.Body:
**Version Used**: .NET SDK 10.0.400; Roslyn 5.9.0-1.26379.115 (14fbf8d5271c98133561eb55185fdb05b286f578); Windows 11 x64 **Steps to Reproduce**: 1. Create `encdyn.csproj` and `Program.cs` as below. 2. `dotnet watch run` 3. Uncomment the `Commands.Add(async ct => await model.Increment(ct));` line and save. ```xml Exe net10.0 enable enable ``` ```csharp var model = new Model(); var vm = new ViewModel(); while (true) { vm.Initialize(model); foreach (var c in vm.Commands) await c(default); Console.WriteLine($"tick commands={vm.Commands.Count} count={model.Count}"); await Task.Delay(1000); } public class Model { public int Count; public async Task Increment(CancellationToken ct) { await Task.Yield(); Count++; } } public class ViewModel { public readonly List> Feeds = new(); public readonly List> Commands = new(); public void Initialize(object updatedModel) { dynamic model = updatedModel; Feeds.Clear(); Commands.Clear(); Feeds.Add(() => model.Count); // a lambda already captures the dynamic local // Hot Reload edit: uncomment the next line and save. // Commands.Add(async ct => await model.Increment(ct)); } } ``` **Expected Behavior**: The edit applies, or is reported as an unsupported edit. Either way, `dotnet watch` keeps running. **Actual Behavior**: `dotnet watch` stops the app and exits: ``` dotnet watch : An unexpected error occurred: System.InvalidOperationException: Unexpected value 'ViewModel.<>c__DisplayClass2_0.<b__1#1>d.<>o.<>p__0' of type 'Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Symbols.SynthesizedFieldSymbol' at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Emit.DeltaMetadataWriter.DefinitionIndexBase`1.GetRowId(T item) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Emit.DeltaMetadataWriter.GetFieldDefinitionHandle(IFieldDefinition def) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.GetFieldHandle(IFieldReference fieldReference) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.GetHandle(Object reference) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.ResolveEntityHandleFromPseudoToken(Int32 pseudoSymbolToken) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.WriteInstructions(...) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.SerializeMethodBody(...) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.SerializeMethodBodies(...) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.BuildMetadataAndIL(...) at Microsoft.Cci.MetadataWriter.WriteMetadataAndIL(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.SerializeToDeltaStreams(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Emit.EmitHelpers.EmitDifference(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Compilation.EmitDifference(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.EditAndContinue.EditSession.EmitSolutionUpdateAsync(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.EditAndContinue.DebuggingSession.EmitSolutionUpdateAsync(...) at Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.ExternalAccess.HotReload.Api.HotReloadService.GetUpdatesAsync(...) at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.ProjectUpdatesBuilder.AddManagedCodeUpdatesAsync(...) ``` The field is a dynamic call-site container field (`<>o.<>p__0`) nested in the new lambda's async state machine; awaiting a `dynamic` value is what puts the awaiter's call sites (`GetAwaiter`, `IsCompleted`, `GetResult`) there. It is synthesized in this generation, but the delta writer finds no row for it.
Full dotnet watch output ``` dotnet watch 🔥 Hot reload enabled. For a list of supported edits, see https://aka.ms/dotnet/hot-reload. dotnet watch 💡 Press Ctrl+R to restart. CancellationToken cancellationToken) at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.HotReloadDotNetWatcher.WatchAsync(CancellationToken shutdownCancellationToken) at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.HotReloadDotNetWatcher.WatchAsync(CancellationToken shutdownCancellationToken) at Microsoft.DotNet.Watch.Program.RunAsync() ```
**What triggers it** Each variant is one edit to the baseline above (an existing lambda captures `dynamic model`): | Added lambda | Result | |---|---| | `async ct => await model.Increment(ct)` (awaits a `dynamic` value) | **crash** | | `async ct => await (Task)model.Increment(ct)` (dynamic call, awaits a `Task`) | applied | | `async ct => await Task.Yield()` (async, no dynamic) | applied | | `ct => (Task)model.Increment(ct)` (dynamic, not async) | applied | | async + dynamic, with no other lambda capturing `model` in the baseline | applied | In Uno Platform's generated code (below), changing the parameter list of an existing async lambda that awaits a `dynamic` call also crashes with this exception. I haven't reduced that variant to the console repro. **Impact** Uno Platform's MVUX source generator emits exactly this shape for Hot Reload: `dynamic model = updatedModel;` plus one async lambda per command overload that awaits `model.Command(...)`. Changing a command's parameters therefore crashes the EnC session in Uno's DevServer. Uno's DevServer then reports InternalError for that edit and for every later one until the app restarts. In three AI-agent runs of a simple counter app, this cost about one restart per run.

Issues.Title: Test_Windows_CoreClr_Debug_Single_Machine: 120-min job timeout from LanguageServer.UnitTests_38 global deadline
Issues.Body:
## Build Information
Build: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1634003
Leg Name: Test_Windows_CoreClr_Debug_Single_Machine

## Description
The `Test_Windows_CoreClr_Debug_Single_Machine` job on `roslyn-CI` (definition 95) repeatedly exceeds the
120-minute Azure Pipelines job timeout while running `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.LanguageServer.UnitTests_38`.
The "Run Unit Tests" step reports a global test timeout and collects owned work-item dumps before
termination, then the AzDO agent kills the job for exceeding the max time.

Observed on `refs/heads/main` CI builds over the last several days (recurring, not isolated to a single
commit or PR):
- https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1630480 (2026-10-10)

Issues.Title: [15.9] Backport DevDiv engineering feed WIF authentication (#83918)
Issues.Body:
AI-generated:

Manual backport of #83918 to `release/dev15.9.x`, addressing the [failed automated backport](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/83918#issuecomment-6154593884).

<details><summary>Ask Mode template completed</summary>

<!-- This template is not always required. If you aren't sure about whether it's needed or want help filling out the sections,
submit the pull request and then ask us for help. :) -->

### Customer scenario

Official builds of `release/dev15.9.x` authenticate to the DevDiv Engineering NuGet feed using a PAT-based service connection. This backport applies the merged WIF migration without overwriting the release-specific pipeline configuration.

### Bugs this fixes

Backports #83918 (merge commit `792f89c9d75a8358d228ddeaed402799f37440a6`). The [automated backport failed](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/83918#issuecomment-6154593884) because `azure-pipelines-official.yml` differs from main.

Related work item: https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_workitems/edit/10126

### Workarounds, if any

Retaining PAT-based authentication does not complete the requested WIF migration. A manual backport is required to preserve the release-specific authentication tasks.

### Risk

Limited to official-build feed authentication. Remove only `devdiv/engineering` from `nuGetServiceConnections`, retaining `devdiv/dotnet-core-internal-tooling`. Add a separate `NuGetAuthenticate@1` task with `azureDevOpsServiceConnection: devdiv-engineering-feed-r-wif` and `feedUrl: https://devdiv.pkgs.visualstudio.com/_packaging/Engineering/nuget/v3/index.json`. Existing azure-public and CoreXT WIF authentication, build settings, signing, and publishing remain unchanged.

### Performance impact

One additional authentication task in the official pipeline; no compiler or IDE runtime changes.

### Is this a regression from a previous update?

No product regression. This addresses an automated backport conflict for the merged migration.

### Root cause analysis

The source patch assumes main's combined legacy feed list, but 15.9 already authenticates azure-public and CoreXT feeds in separate WIF tasks. The manual backport preserves those tasks and migrates only the Engineering feed.

Validation: `git diff --check` passed. An inline Python script using `yaml.safe_load` parsed both the release baseline and modified YAML, then asserted full-document equality against a baseline modified only by removing the Engineering PAT connection and inserting the exact WIF task. It also checked the task occurs once, precedes restore, and the legacy Engineering connection is absent; all assertions passed.

Live Azure DevOps pipeline validation and WIF authentication were not exercised locally. No product unit tests were run because the change affects pipeline YAML only; official-pipeline execution remains necessary to verify service-connection authorization and feed access.

### How was the bug found?

The automated backport reported conflicts in both cherry-pick and `git am`: https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/83918#issuecomment-6154593884.

### Test documentation updated?

Not applicable: this is build infrastructure, not a new product feature. No manual-testing documentation changes are needed.

If this is a new non-compiler feature or a significant improvement to an existing feature, update https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/wiki/Manual-Testing once you know which release it is targeting.

</details>

Issues.Title: [release/dev17.14] Fix MSBuildWorkspace DisposeAsync type-load failures
Issues.Body:
AI-generated:

Addresses #85848 for `release/dev17.14` and fixes the 165 failures in [roslyn-CI run 20261012.1](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1631694).

All 165 failures are in `VisualStudioMSBuildWorkspaceTests` and contain the same `ProjectCacheService.DisposeAsync` type-load error, including the three exception-assertion failures and the aggregate exception.

The .NET Framework BuildHost ships `System.Threading.Tasks.Extensions` 4.5.4 (assembly 4.2.0.1). Newer MSBuild dependencies can resolve `ValueTask` from assembly 4.2.4.0, causing the implementation and `IAsyncDisposable` interface signatures to disagree. Update only this host to Tasks.Extensions 4.6.3 and its required Unsafe 6.1.2 dependency, and reuse `GenerateCompilerExecutableBindingRedirects.targets` to unify older references from dynamically loaded MSBuild. The .NET Core host and repository-wide package versions are unchanged.

## CI validation completed

- [Standard PR CI, build 1634175](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1634175): all build, analyzer, source-build, and test checks passed. Azure DevOps reports `partiallySucceeded` solely because the non-blocking Publish Logs task could not read a locked `Build.Server.log`; the GitHub check is successful.
- Standard PR CI excludes the original failing single-machine leg, so I also queued [branch validation, build 1634220](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng-public/public/_build/results?buildId=1634220) on the exact fixing commit. This run completed **succeeded**, including `Test_Windows_CoreClr_Debug_Single_Machine`.
- Single-machine test run: **170,321 passed, 0 failed, 1,150 skipped**, versus the original **170,156 passed, 165 failed, 1,150 skipped**. The total remains 171,471: all 165 failures became passes without increasing skips.
- The single-machine log explicitly reports `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.UnitTests_36 PASSED` and `All tests passed`.
- All active PR checks, Build Analysis, and Build Insights are successful. Integration CI is neutral because trigger conditions excluded it. No review comments are outstanding. PR remains draft.

## Local validation

- Pinned SDK 9.0.121; `dotnet test src\Workspaces\MSBuild\Test\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.UnitTests.csproj -f net9.0 --filter FullyQualifiedName~VisualStudioMSBuildWorkspaceTests.TestOpenSolution_SingleProjectSolution` rebuilt and failed before the fix with the exact CI exception, then passed after the fix.
- Reproduction used an isolated MSBuild.Runtime 17.14.28 deployment with Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces 10.0.10 and Tasks.Extensions 4.6.3; the same deployment was retained for the before/after comparison.
- `dotnet build src\Workspaces\MSBuild\BuildHost\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.BuildHost.csproj --no-restore -p:RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`: passed for both host frameworks, zero warnings/errors.
- Confirmed generated net472 configuration redirects Tasks.Extensions 0.0.0.0–4.2.4.0 to 4.2.4.0.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Documentation assessed; no contributor guidance or public API change is needed.

The full local project run was stopped because installed Visual Studio 18 fails independently in `XMakeElements` before and after this fix, while the isolated deployment lacks complete Visual Studio design-time behavior and produced metadata-reference assertion failures. Complete CI validation above supersedes that local environment limitation.

Issues.Title: Fix Generate Constructor crash when inspecting properties in referenced projects
Issues.Body:
Fixes dotnet/roslyn#82157.

Generate Constructor can inspect a getter-only property declared in a referenced project to determine whether it is a `NotImplementedException` stub. Previously, this check requested a semantic model from the calling project’s compilation for the property’s syntax tree, throwing `ArgumentException: SyntaxTree is not part of the compilation` and causing Visual Studio to disable the provider.

Check that accessor syntax trees belong to the supplied compilation before requesting semantic models. Properties outside that compilation are not treated as reusable stubs, allowing constructor generation to create a new field instead. Also restrict accessor analysis to the current syntax-tree group.

Issues.Title: Escaping more quotation marks in PowerShell help descriptions.
Issues.Body:
Reopen #55040. The fix is still relevant and I'd like to see it land in the .NET 11 in next month if possible. Thanks!

Currently, the `SanitizeHelpDescription` function does not escape curly quotes `“` and `”`. However, PowerShell utilizes "smart quotes", which causes it to mistakenly interpret curly quotes within Simplified Chinese command descriptions as string delimiters, breaking the PowerShell completions script.

This PR adds escaping for `“` and `”` to resolve the PowerShell string delimiting issue. Additionally, it escapes `„`, which should help prevent similar issues with PowerShell completion in languages like German.

Since we surround command descriptions with double quotes (`"`), escaping single quotes (`'`) should be unnecessary.

Fix: #51260

Issues.Title: CA2000 false positive when a disposable is passed to a primary constructor and stored
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

If a disposable is passed to a primary constructor that stores it, CA2000 reports a leak where the disposable is created. That's true whether it's stored through a property initializer, a field initializer or a captured parameter. The same code with an explicit constructor reports nothing. This looks like the CA2000 counterpart of dotnet/roslyn-analyzers#7803 (CA2213): the analyzer doesn't see the primary constructor's initializers when it follows the call into the constructor.

### Steps to reproduce

.editorconfig: `dotnet_diagnostic.CA2000.severity = warning`

```csharp
public sealed class Res : IDisposable { public void Dispose() { } }

public sealed class Explicit
{
    public Explicit(Res r) { R = r; }
    public Res R { get; }
}

public sealed class PrimaryProperty(Res r) { public Res R { get; } = r; }
public sealed class PrimaryField(Res r) { private readonly Res _r = r; public Res R => _r; }
public sealed class PrimaryCaptured(Res r) { public Res R => r; }

public static class Use
{
    public static Explicit A() => new(new Res());        // no diagnostic
    public static PrimaryProperty B() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
    public static PrimaryField C() => new(new Res());    // CA2000
    public static PrimaryCaptured D() => new(new Res()); // CA2000
}
```

### Expected behavior

None of the four call sites gets a diagnostic. In each case the object is handed to the new instance, which stores it.

### Actual behavior

B, C and D report CA2000: Call `System.IDisposable.Dispose` on object created by 'new Res()' before all references to it are out of scope. A doesn't.

### Is this a regression?

_No response_

### Are there any workarounds?

Use an explicit constructor, or suppress CA2000 at the call site.

Issues.Title: Build daily and preview dotnetup candidates in one CI run
Issues.Body:
## Summary

We'd like to be able to produce two sets of dotnetup artifacts with the same build, using different version numbers for different channels. That way when we want to promote a build from the daily to the preview channel, we don't have to do a rebuild, but we can tell which channel was installed.

This requires the changes from https://github.com/dotnet/arcade/pull/17695.

## AI Description

Build daily- and preview-stamped dotnetup candidates from the same commit in one CI run, and register each candidate as a separate BAR build.

This lets us publish daily builds automatically and later promote an already-built preview candidate without rebuilding or maintaining a separate preview branch. Because the channel-specific version is embedded in the binaries, preview promotion selects the prebuilt preview candidate rather than restamping the daily binary.

## Changes

- Build both candidates sequentially on each existing RID agent, with isolated intermediate and output directories.
- Generate and upload separate V4 manifests and artifacts for each candidate.
- Use two standard Arcade registration jobs: daily publishes automatically for eligible builds; preview registers without immediate publication.
- Preserve existing behavior for SDK build jobs that do not specify variants.
- Document preview candidate selection and promotion.

Manifest generation, merging, registration, and publication remain owned by Arcade. This does not introduce an SDK manifest splitter, artifact allowlist, or CDN change.

## Dependencies

Requires the companion Arcade changes for variant registration and BAR-record-based manifest discovery. The Arcade package/shared-template update and promotion-pipeline rollout must land before enabling this pipeline change.

The dependency pin is intentionally unchanged in this proposal.

Issues.Title: Check each referenced project once in dotnet format
Issues.Body:
Fixes #56363

### Problem

Before running analyzers, `AnalyzerRunner.RunCodeAnalysisAsync` checks that every referenced project's compilation loaded by recursively walking `ProjectReferences`. The walk never remembers which projects it already verified, so a shared dependency is re-walked once per path that reaches it. The cost grows exponentially with the depth of the reference graph, which makes `dotnet format style` / `dotnet format analyzers` take minutes to hours on solutions with dense reference graphs (for example, ones using `DisableTransitiveProjectReferences`).

### Fix

Replace the recursive walk with a single pass over the project and its transitive dependencies, taken from the solution's cached `ProjectDependencyGraph` (`GetProjectsThatThisProjectTransitivelyDependsOn`). Each project's compilation is checked exactly once, with no recursion. Any dependency that fails to load still skips the project with the existing "required references did not load" warning.

### Tests

Added `AnalyzerRunnerTests`:

- `RunCodeAnalysisAsync_DenseProjectReferenceGraph_CompletesPromptly`: 40 projects, each referencing every earlier one. Without the fix it does not finish within the 60 s timeout; with the fix it completes in a few seconds.
- `RunCodeAnalysisAsync_SharedReferenceMissingCorlib_SkipsProject`: a shared dependency in the middle of the graph is missing corlib; the top project is still skipped with the "required references did not load" warning.
- `RunCodeAnalysisAsync_IndirectReferenceMissingCorlib_SkipsProject`: a three-project chain where the broken project is reachable from the top project only transitively; guards against checking direct references alone.

Locally, the rest of `dotnet-format.UnitTests` is unchanged by this PR. (Tests that need a built `redist` layout were not run locally, and `TestUseVarCodeStyle_AppliesWhenNotUsingVar` fails on `main` with or without this change.)

### Servicing

The same unmemoized recursion exists in the `release/10.0.*xx` branches, but in a different form: a synchronous `AllReferencedProjectsLoaded` that checks for an `mscorlib.dll` metadata reference, under `src/BuiltInTools/dotnet-format` in 10.0.1xx/2xx. So this won't cherry-pick cleanly and needs a manual port. Would maintainers consider servicing this fix into .NET 10? I'm happy to prepare the backport PR(s).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Check each referenced project once in dotnet format" (#56621)

Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK file-based apps. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Signature verification for .NET file-based apps can fail to enforce the expected trust decision. ## Announcement Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/487 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-347 (Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Issues.Title: .NET 11 Release Candidate 2
Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of [dotnet/core/discussions/10644](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10644). See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 2. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc2).

This is our second of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc2/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-96960 | .NET and Visual Studio Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Security.Cryptography.Xml; System.Private.Xml. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Signed XML fixes add input-depth and operation-count limits, prohibit DTD processing by default, validate entity references, bound encrypted-data candidate processing, and cap attributes and namespaces used by C14N transforms. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135711 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-405 (Asymmetric Resource Consumption (Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 8.0, you should download and install .NET 8.0.32 Runtime or .NET 8.0.426 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/8.0. * If you're using .NET 9.0, you should download and install .NET 9.0.21 Runtime or .NET 9.0.319 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/9.0. * If you're using .NET 10.0, you should download and install .NET 10.0.13 Runtime or .NET 10.0.402 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/10.0. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime; System.Private.CoreLib. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Unix named-mutex and shared-memory paths can be manipulated through insecure global directories, symlink races, and unsafe permission changes, allowing local attackers to truncate or overwrite files, widen directory permissions, or elevate privileges. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135707 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in System.Net.Security. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. .NET 11 post-handshake TLS client authentication can fail to verify the client certificate, allowing mutual-authentication requirements to be bypassed. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135701 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Moderate - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-295 (Improper Certificate Validation) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, <= 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. * If you're using .NET 11.0, you should download and install .NET 11.0.0-rc.2 Runtime or .NET 11.0.100-rc.2 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet-core/11.0. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-70194](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-70194) ### Acknowledgements - Kirill Mitrofanov ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70190 | .NET SDK Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK workload installation and advertising manifests. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The elevated SDK workload installer can follow a junction or symlink under `%ProgramData%\dotnet`, enabling local privilege escalation. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56612 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-59 (Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | --------------- .NET SDK | >= 11.0.100-preview.1, <= 11.0.100-rc.1 | 11.0.100-rc.2 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.401 | 10.0.402 .NET SDK | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.112 | 10.0.113 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-70190](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-70190) ### Acknowledgements - Coşkun Bağrıaçık ### Revisions V1.0 (10/13/2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-70188 | ASP.NET Core Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Kestrel accepts newline characters in HTTP/2 request trailers and values retrieved from the dynamic HPACK table instead of treating them as malformed. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69798 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-444 (Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects Microsoft .NET projects that use an affected package version listed below.
